top_signal.title: Help Disabled Entrepreneurs Get the Startup Capital They Deserve
top_signal.summary: Here's the problem: disabled folks on SSI benefits often have amazing business ideas—web design, crafts, digital content—but no money to actually start them. The SSA's PASS program is supposed to help by letting you set aside income for business costs without losing benefits. But here's the catch: you need money to set aside in the first place. Most people on disability don't have spare cash, so they stay stuck.   I started a petition asking Congress and the IRS to create a $10,000 refundable tax credit specifically for disabled entrepreneurs, and to make it work directly with the PASS program. The idea is simple: the IRS provides the seed capital, the SSA makes sure it's spent on actual business costs (equipment, education, supplies, marketing), and disabled people finally get a real shot at building something sustainable instead of staying dependent on benefits.   It's not charity—it's an investment in people who want to work but just need that initial push. Has anyone here tried starting a business while on disability, or seen how hard it is? If this feels like something that should exist, consider signing and sharing it. Real change happens when people speak up about what actually works.        submitted by     /u/Normal-Put9661       [link]       [comments]
